changeSet.author: spike-gmail
changeSet.comment: Schema required by Spring Security's JdbcOAuth2AuthorizedClientService (oauth2-client-schema.sql). This is where the admin's Gmail access and refresh tokens are stored.

sql.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oauth2_authorized_client (client_registration_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, principal_name varchar(200) NOT NULL, access_token_type varchar(100) NOT NULL, access_token_value blob NOT NULL, access_token_issued_at timestamp NOT NULL, access_token_expires_at timestamp NOT NULL, access_token_scopes varchar(1000) DEFAULT NULL, refresh_token_value blob DEFAULT NULL, refresh_token_issued_at timestamp DEFAULT NULL, created_at timestamp DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (client_registration_id, principal_name))

changeSet.author: spike-gmail
changeSet.comment: Same schema as the H2 changeSet, but PostgreSQL has no blob column type; bytea is what Spring Security's documentation recommends.

sql.sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS oauth2_authorized_client (client_registration_id varchar(100) NOT NULL, principal_name varchar(200) NOT NULL, access_token_type varchar(100) NOT NULL, access_token_value bytea NOT NULL, access_token_issued_at timestamp NOT NULL, access_token_expires_at timestamp NOT NULL, access_token_scopes varchar(1000) DEFAULT NULL, refresh_token_value bytea DEFAULT NULL, refresh_token_issued_at timestamp DEFAULT NULL, created_at timestamp DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (client_registration_id, principal_name))
